items.title: 66096_Monk Montgomery oral history interview
items.q: The tenor player, Pookie, was just a great player.

ctx.x: No, they weren't related, but their last names were the same. So we decided that the best way to title the group was the Montgomery-Johnsons. Not "Brothers," but the Montgomery-Johnson Quintet. The tenor player, Pookie, was just a great player. He and Wes, the front line, played so well together, because they dug each other and they (unintelligible) the music. So all the things worked out with tenor and guitar.

And what a sound it was, because when those guys played ensembles and heads of tunes, they sounded like one instrument, the phrasing and everything was so close together, it sounded like a different sound, but one instrument. It was just that close, and they both played so good together.
